decisions.statement: The seconds a command is allowed are read off that command's own page.
A page stating no seconds is allowed the seconds this module names.
A page stating seconds that are neither null nor a number above nothing is allowed the same.
A page stating null for its seconds runs under no ceiling.
A call under no ceiling is watched by no thread at all.
The seconds are counted on the wall clock rather than on the work a command does.
The watch runs on a thread of its own.
A command with the loop for its whole run is stopped all the same.
What is said names the call and the seconds that call was allowed.
What is said sends a ceiling that wants raising to Alan.
A stopped call says why on the error stream and the process is ended.
A call answering inside its seconds ends the watch.
One watch is live at a time.
Ending the watch ends whichever watch is live rather than the watch first started.
A call may be allowed more seconds while that call runs.
Allowing more seconds ends the watch that was live and starts a watch for those seconds.
A call allowed more seconds where no watch is live is left with no watch.
A call may be allowed the rest of its run under no ceiling.
Allowing a call through ends the watch that was live.
A call stopped at the ceiling records nothing about what that call cost.
Nothing here waits on the answer a command gives.

definition: a call stopped where the command runs past the seconds that command is allowed
